To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NMDA-type glutamate receptors are involved in the mechanism that controls the plasticity of the sensory input from the head skin chemoreceptors to the snail’s defensive behavior command neurons.
the NMDA-like receptors are selectively involved only in the induction of the plasticity of the synaptic inputs to the command neurons, excited by chemical stimulation of skin receptors of the head.

the NMDA glutamatergic system is selectively involved in the induction of plasticity in synaptic inputs from chemoreceptors in the snail's skin to command neurons LPI1 and RPI1, excited by sensory stimulation of the snails' head, during acquisition of nocicpetive sensitization in the snail Helix lucorum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of the formation of the sensitized state and its maintenance, as well as the role of glutamate in these processes.

a new approach to the study of mechanisms of the induction of long-term sensitization of nociceptive behavior in the snail, based on a selective effect of the NMDA receptor antagonist MK-801 on the plasticity induced by sensitizing stimuli in sensory inputs to the defensive behavior command neurons.
the role of NMDA-like receptors in the induction of plasticity at synapses with command neurons during acquisition of sensitization to noxious stimuli in snails.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MK-801, a non-competitive NMDA antagonist, is capable of blocking sensitization of the defensive response in the snail.

NMDA glutamatergic receptors are selectively involved into the mechanisms of induction of synaptic plasticity of the inputs from skin chemoreceptors of the snail head to command neurons LPI1 and RPI1 during acquisition of the nociceptive sensitisation.
the effects of NMDA receptor antagonist MK-801 are specific for the induction of plasticity in the sensory inputs to LPl1 and RP11 neurons excited by chemical stimulation of head skin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NMDA receptors are involved in the mechanism that induces long-term plasticity in the snail's nociceptive system.
the NMDA glutamatergic receptor is involved in the process of nociceptive plasticity in the CNS of the snail.

NMDA glutamine receptors are selectively involved only in the mechanism of acquisition of sensitization to the head, and the acquisition of sensitization in other skin receptor zones is mediated by other mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the selective involvement of NMDA-like receptors in the induction of plastic changes in the sensory inputs to command neurons is a feature common to different types of sensitization in the snail.

NMDA glutamatergic receptors play an essential role in the acquisition of long-lasting changes in the excitability of neurons of the defensive behavior command center of snails during the induction of sensitization.
the NMDA-like receptors in the brain are involved in the induction of plasticity at the synapses of the sensory neurons excited by the chemical stimulation of the skin of the snail head.
